changes_from_redteam: [better-in-every-sense, critical] User flow broke at telephony (BYO-only v1). Fixed: in-product rental in the tenant's name through a carrier partner is now decision 6 (Vobiz rentals inside Sarvam and Bolna are the observed precedent), asked in the KC5 quote round (~2026-10-30); BYO is the second path; VP Success assisted onboarding added; W7b (first production call, KYC included) added. Terms stay [U] until carriers answer. (§1, §5, §6.7, §11, §12)

[better-in-every-sense, critical] BFSI beachhead vs non-resident default stack. Fixed: sector packs (IRDAI, RBI) carry an India-resident call stack, analysis model and Operator brain priced by the Base margin rule, not Premium-only; BFSI workspaces use India-resident Operator brains only. (§6.1, §8.3)

[better-in-every-sense, critical] Results unverifiable for SMBs without webhooks. Fixed: no-developer outcome sources (paid-list re-upload or Sheet column, insurer MIS file parser, manager confirmation graded below system-verified) plus interim metrics (promise with date, callback booked, agenda done, link opened); 10-15 buyer interviews are a Phase 0 gate. (§6.4, §11, §12)

[better-in-every-sense + feasibility, critical] First jobs depend on KC5 (1600 streaming) and KC8 (solicitation). Fixed: v0.5 starts with a non-BFSI partner on a declared 10-digit line; appointment and subscription presets ship first; insurance and lending presets are gated on KC5 and counsel; no IRDAI-pack build before counsel. (§3, §6.3, §11)

[feasibility, critical] No buildable v1 (rejected.harvest.19). Fixed: a v0.5 vertical slice (one non-BFSI preset, one carrier path, one measured stack; hear-it-first to call page) with exit bars (W1 on carrier CDRs, W2, W6, W7, the joint speed gate, load test, 30 days of zero-ring audits, 3 partners with outcomes, pen test); every other item waits behind it. (P13, §11)

[feasibility, critical] Speed vs voice; predicted gap used a 304 ms TTFT measured on a smaller warm prompt. Fixed: gaps recomputed with brief-v2 TTFT (567-641 ms, n=5-6): Natural predicted 2.0-2.5 s at the handset, Fast 1.6-2.0 s, Indic 1.2-1.6 s; speed and cut-ins are one joint gate at the handset; the default is the best whole-call ear rating among passing stacks; Natural is opt-in with its wait shown (open decision 1). Not fixable by design alone: no stack passes the cut-in bar today. (§1 decision 4, §8.1-8.2)

[better-in-every-sense, major] Natural proposed as default despite missing the bar. Fixed by the joint gate above; the turn-taking battery is a hard v0.5 exit and Phase 0 gate (~2026-11-06). (§8.2, §11)

[better-in-every-sense, major] Catalogue could not contain the best voices. Partly fixed: ElevenLabs and Cartesia are proposed as benchmark rows in the round-2 whole-call ear test (open decision 11). Not fixed: the dedicated brand voice stays Premium/v2 because its approval is unverified and it costs INR 3.5 lakh a month. (§8.3, §14)

[better-in-every-sense + feasibility, major] All-in per-second billing contradicted BYO, where the carrier bills the tenant. Fixed: two billing modes; on BYO, VP bills a platform rate (all-in minus the INR 0.45 telephony allowance) and shows the computed all-in total and effective rate at the carrier's pulse; W8/T7 judged on the sum of both invoices until counsel allows one invoice. (§6.8)

[better-in-every-sense + feasibility, major] Per-minute launch pricing contradicted rejected.2026-10-17.per-minute-launch. Fixed: a proposed decision supersedes it for self-serve scope only (buyer staffs escalation, carriers bill 1600, WhatsApp at cost) with reverse_if (INT proposed_graph_entries); no price printed until re-metered; per-outcome pricing restated as a software fee while the tenant runs its own number and humans. (§8.3, open decision 2)

[better-in-every-sense + feasibility, major] Margins left out fixed and acquisition costs and used a lean-persona AI cost. Fixed: the x1.3 persona-and-memory uplift applied (Natural COGS ~2.57, 3.04 in 2027); Base shown as INR 3.49-3.99 provisional; the fixed-cost layer is named (Operator, tests, monitoring, support, disputes); trial capped at INR 500 lifetime per verified phone; recovery is open decision 12. (§8.3)

[integrator, found in final check] The Base rule had no answer when the ear's pick needs more than 3.99 (Natural from 2027-01-01 needs about 4.16; Fast if MAI bills like HD). Fixed: the voice is kept and the owner chooses a 4.49 step or a lower 2027 margin; stated in §8.3 and open decision 2.

[better-in-every-sense, major] 'Cheaper than everyone' overclaimed. Fixed: the only cost claim is 'the lowest effective price on short calls, per second, with caps', allowed only after the T7 invoice audit; Sarvam Business (whole minutes) and claimed SquadStack/Bolna floors are stated; no price-led hero. (§8.5, §9)

[better-in-every-sense, major] v1 lacked regional languages (req-10). Fixed in part: five regional betas (Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Marathi, Bengali) in v1 on the Indic stack, each gated on its own opt-out, crisis, disclosure and goodbye lexicons and ≥ 95% language hold; GA in v2; the loss to Sarvam on languages is stated. (§6.2, §9)

[better-in-every-sense, major] Parity holes (flows, agent hand-off, text channels, generic SIP, custom LLM, concurrency). Fixed in part: a stages layer plus agent-to-agent hand-off, proven on a new T10 branching task before any graph builder; custom-LLM endpoint in v1; Base concurrency raised to 20 (Retell's free floor). Deferred with reason: generic SIP and WhatsApp conversational agents in v2, Telegram v3 (req-67 is nice-priority). (§6.3, §6.8, §9, §11)

[better-in-every-sense + feasibility, major] Four conflicting disclosure placements; turn 2 overloaded; no lawful control for the disclosure test. Fixed: one opening spec owned by voice and checked by trust (name check; then her name, brand, 'AI assistant' in passing, useful fact); 'spent only when heard' resolves RD1 vs R4; recording notice moved to her next content turn; the test is a placement A/B plus hazard at the disclosure moment, never an undisclosed arm; reversal if counsel requires the clause in the first words. (§6.2, §11, App B, open decision 16)

[better-in-every-sense, major] Self-learning promise contradicted by copy rules. Put to the owner: a bounded standing approval envelope in v2 and the copy 'improves itself within limits you set, and proves what it changes' (open decision 5). (§5, §6.6)

[better-in-every-sense, major] Statistics and internals shown to an owner on a phone. Fixed: Owner view by default for Owners and Viewers; Expert view for Builders, Compliance and Developers; same objects, no hidden safety states. (§3, §6.9)

[better-in-every-sense, major] SquadStack's human CSMs beat 'just talk'. Fixed: VP Success assisted onboarding (IST hours) acting only through the same tools and ledger, included for the first 10-20 tenants; the unassisted share is tracked. (§5, open decision 15)

[better-in-every-sense, major] W7 was a vanity metric. Fixed: W7 is measured on Bolna and Sarvam with a stopwatch; W7b (sign-up to the first production call from the tenant's declared line, KYC included) added; competitors' ring time graded [U]. (§4.4, §11, §12)
[better-in-every-sense, major] Registry missed actions other modules defined. Fixed: 17 tools added with risk classes (INT registry_additions), CI parity check across module screens. (§6.1)
[better-in-every-sense, major] v1 scope repeated rejected.harvest.19. Fixed by the v0.5 slice (see the feasibility critical item). (§11)

[feasibility, major] Reply-door classifier predicates had unmeasured errors and latency. Fixed: each predicate labelled deterministic or classifier-based; risky turns hold the whole reply; a blocked later clause plays a pre-rendered bridge then regenerates; a Phase 0 battery measures false positives, false negatives and added latency; model-based fences ship only after measured recall. (§6.2, §11)

[feasibility, major] Echo evidence (0/66) came from Azure Voice Live preview on a simulated harness. Fixed: no longer cited as VP evidence; VP builds reference echo handling against its own outbound audio and tests it on the Plivo leg with real handsets and speakerphones. (§6.2)

[feasibility, major] W3 could not be computed. Fixed: an absolute handset bar (p50 ≤ 1.5 s, p90 ≤ 2.5 s, cut-ins ≤ 5%) is the pass condition; Bolna and Sarvam are measured on the same handset before any comparative claim; the Plivo recharge before 2026-11-16 is an owner decision. (§9, §11, open decision 13)

[feasibility, major] Voice quality rested on text-only measures. Fixed: Phase 0 adds agenda completion per simulated call scored against hidden keys beside whole-call human ratings; if no stack reaches 7.0, the best-rated passing stack ships with its rating shown. (§11, open decision 1)

[feasibility, major] Self-learning targets did not fit the arithmetic. Fixed: first proved change within 30 days only for turn-taking; any slot 60-90 days at L2; probes ≥ 60 runs per arm with the reference spread measured on ≥ 2 pairs; FDR control on drop-off flags; test budget matched to one cycle a day (two on Plus at INR 400). (§6.4, §6.6)

[feasibility, major] Auto-revert could republish a stale version. Fixed: deployment.revert_to_last_good is an explicit A3 verb allowed only if the previous version ran 200+ clean calls and re-passes today's compile, lint, locked-section, provenance and fact checks; otherwise a 25% throttle and a card. (§5)

[feasibility, major] Predial hook inside the claim transaction broke the 50 ms precheck. Fixed: two-phase reserve, veto outside the transaction, confirm or release; one timeout (800 ms) in the defaults registry. (§6.3, App B)

[feasibility, major] Failure modes under-designed. Fixed: pre-rendered hold and close clips per voice at publish; a cross-provider declared alternate before production; VP-owned Google organisation and Vertex project with measured quotas; a voice-rt load test, India DR (RPO ≤ 15 min, RTO ≤ 4 h) and on-call runbooks before v0.5 exits. (§6.8, §7.2, §7.3)

[feasibility, major] Security gaps. Fixed: in-call tool arguments bound to the dialled contact's record keys; an egress allowlist with private-range blocking for every tenant URL; the Operator sees receipts, headers and value shapes, never raw rows; free minutes capped per verified phone; credential rotation is a v0.5 entry condition; a penetration test before production. (§6.1, §6.7, §11)

[feasibility, major] Identity disclosed before verification. Fixed: a knowledge check before account details or memory on inbound, lending outbound and when a relative answers; generic callback openers; no call purpose on the verify page for lending and collections. (§6.3, §6.5, §6.7)

[feasibility, major] Rejected ideas re-proposed without edges. Fixed: per-minute pricing superseded only for self-serve with reverse_if; price-led hero removed; per-outcome restated as a software fee; the Premium Live gate now needs the transcript lead-time distribution and buffered latency, not a count. (§8.2, §8.3, §8.5, INT)

[feasibility, major] Self-serve built without buyer evidence; support uncosted. Fixed: 10-15 buyer interviews in Phase 0 before self-serve-only surfaces; support priced into the fixed-cost layer. (§10, §11, open decision 12)
[feasibility, major] VP's own DLT registration and trial-line A2P declaration missing from the critical path. Fixed: dated Phase 0 task due 2026-11-14. (§6.7, §11)

[minor] Tiers: preferences in Base, relational memory in Plus. Autonomy: explicit revert verb. Defaults: Appendix B names one owner per default with a CI check. Shell and name: 'VP' in v0.5, the design-language shell. (§5, App B)

[minor] Case table extended: bereavement, a new number offered, unsupported language, a minor answering, 'WhatsApp pe bhej do', a third party asking for account details, mid-call tool or provider failure. (§4.11)

[minor] Claims hygiene: Bolna's 'hidden hold', Retell's batch-DNC claim and 'nobody owns the Hinglish call' were dropped; W7 competitor gap graded [U]; latency always carries its vantage; 'cheaper' stays out of copy until T7. (§1, §4.4, §8.5, §9)
[minor] 'Beyond everyone' inflation: the blueprint leads with ten defining decisions and marks each comparison as beat on paper, match, lose today or unproven, each with its proof. (§1, §9)
[minor] UI proof and animation (req-37): signature moments prototyped as rendered motion for the owner before build; incumbents recorded on video at 390 px before any UI claim. (§6.9)
[minor] Recordings retention: by tier (Base 90 days, Plus 1 year), sector floors (IRDAI 10 years) priced at storage cost. (§6.5, §8.3, App B)

[minor] Redaction by context, checksums only to raise confidence; spam-label and pickup monitoring per line with optional Truecaller verification; DLT SMS and WhatsApp template approvals on the readiness rail with timers; name-check clip cached and intro rendered on answer. (§6.2, §6.3, §6.7)

[minor] Judges calibrated on human quick-rate labels, promise-to-payment tracked separately; VP north star changed to verified earned outcomes per week (minutes are revenue, not the goal); the Operator's voice ear chosen on recorded human commands; simulator prompts framed as QA writing tasks on test quota. (§6.1, §6.4, §6.6, §12)

[minor] Cross-module conflicts resolved: cross-midnight windows refused (quiet hours), person-requested time 07:00-22:00 for service, API key cap INR 2,000/day, trial 5 numbers and 10 rings per number a day, webhook retries 72 h with 30-day replay, Plivo pulse planned at 60 s, Live talk-over ~40%. (App B)

[added from the MISSING lists] 'Predictions' defined (v2 per-contact likelihoods ordering calls, labelled observed; v3 forecasts); scanned-PDF intake by OCR with review (beta); req-57/18 kept as v3; every one of the 68 owner requirements mapped with status. (§6.4, §6.5, App A)

[companion file] Machine-readable resolutions written to /home/user/sales-enabler/data/blueprint/integrator-resolutions.json: opening spec, stack default rule, recomputed gaps, provisional prices and ladder basis, billing modes, v0.5 slice, 17 resolved defaults, 17 registry additions, 17 proposed graph entries (each decision with reverse_if; per-minute supersede scoped to self-serve). Nothing is logged to context/ yet; the main loop merges.

open_decisions.question: Which stack is the default, and what happens when the ear's favourite (Gemini voice) is slower than the speed bar?
open_decisions.recommendation: Let the ear judge whole calls at the handset (≥ 3 testers per stack, stereo battery on Jio, Airtel and Vi). The default is the best-rated stack that passes the joint gate (handset p50 ≤ 1.5 s, p90 ≤ 2.5 s, cut-ins ≤ 5%). Natural (Gemini voice) ships as an opt-in preset with its wait shown until it passes. If no stack passes, ship the best-rated one with its measured numbers shown, fix turn-taking first, and make no speed claim.
options: Natural as default with a stated looser bar (p50 ≤ 2.0 s, cut-ins ≤ 10%)
open_decisions.why: req-01 and req-11 are both must. Natural measured 1.6-2.2 s at the server (smoke, n≈3) and is predicted 2.0-2.5 s at the handset; only Indic is predicted inside 1.5 s; every stack cuts in on 15-42% of turns today.

open_decisions.question: What is the Base price and pricing unit, and how is the INR 2 target handled?
open_decisions.recommendation: Per connected second with an all-in display. Set Base by the margin rule after re-metering the chosen default on the India VM with brief v2, the ledger and a memory brief (INR 3.49-3.99 ex-GST on today's numbers). If the ear's pick needs more than 3.99 (Natural from 2027-01-01, about 4.16; Fast if MAI bills like HD), keep the voice and choose between a 4.49 step and a lower 2027 margin. Sign that v1 launches above INR 2 and reaches it through the pre-registered ladder (2.99 / 2.49 / 1.99 when measured COGS stays at or under 1.94 / 1.62 / 1.29). Log a decision superseding rejected.2026-10-17.per-minute-launch for self-serve scope.
options: Per-second all-in, Base by the margin rule (recommended)
Launch at INR 2.99 and accept under 30% margin
open_decisions.why: req-41 (must, 5 repeats) conflicts with req-02 (voice beats margin): no measured stack reaches INR 2 with a voice that passed the ear test. The old rejection was computed for a managed model in which VP paid human escalation and 1600 carriage.

open_decisions.question: Who are the first design partners?
open_decisions.recommendation: At least one non-BFSI partner (appointment or subscription reminders on a declared 10-digit line) for the v0.5 slice. Insurance renewal and lending pre-due follow only after the KC5 carrier answers (~2026-10-30) and counsel on KC8 (~2026-11-13).
options: Non-BFSI first, BFSI after the gates (recommended)
open_decisions.why: Both lead presets need 1600 numbers. KC5 (AI streaming on 1600) is at risk and KC8 (is a renewal reminder solicitation?) is untested; a negative answer would remove the first preset and the partners.

open_decisions.question: Should VP rent Indian numbers in the tenant's name inside the product, or stay bring-your-own only?
open_decisions.recommendation: Ask Vobiz, Plivo and Exotel in the KC5 quote round for partner or sub-account rental in the tenant's name; ship in-product rental where carrier terms and counsel allow; keep bring-your-own as the second path with guided forms and VP Success.
options: VP as carrier partner of record
open_decisions.why: Sarvam and Bolna already rent Indian numbers inside their products [O]. Bring-your-own only loses the first production call on user flow and convenience. VP must never carry calls itself or become the sender.

open_decisions.question: How does VP honour 'self-learning' (req-34) without a model approving its own changes?
open_decisions.recommendation: Ship the fast lane and fix cards in v1. In v2 add a bounded standing approval envelope: turn timing within preset ranges, middle-slot reorders and objection packs from the approved library auto-start as 10% splits, are promoted only on passing fixed-horizon tests and stop on any guardrail. Adopt the copy 'improves itself within limits you set, and proves what it changes'.
options: Every change one tap; 'self-learning' banned below L4
open_decisions.why: req-34 is must (3 repeats). An opening change needs 686-2,036 calls per arm to prove [C l6] and an objection fix about 600-1,200 calls [I]; daily A/B peeking gave 52-62% false winners in A/A; the competitors' autonomous loops removed the guard.

open_decisions.question: Does preference memory ship in Base (late v1) or wait for v2?
open_decisions.recommendation: Base, late v1, gated by MEM-SIM (recall ≥ 95%, ≤ 1 in 20 preferences ignored) and an India latency A/B (≤ 50 ms added). It slips to v2 if either fails. Relational memory stays in Plus (v2).
open_decisions.why: Retell already ships contact memory, so preferences are parity. The cost is about INR 0.06-0.15 per 3-minute call [C]. req-36 keeps the human voice in Base.

open_decisions.question: What is the Operator called in the product?
open_decisions.recommendation: 'VP' for v0.5; test 'Saarthi' in the 5-user sessions after a brand check.
open_decisions.why: The design module proposed Saarthi while the spine and workspace used VP. A name users mistake for a person would blur VP's own AI honesty.

open_decisions.question: What is the production failover policy (open.2026-10-20.product-failover-policy)?
open_decisions.recommendation: Tests never fall back. At call start, route the whole call to a declared, heard alternate stack on a different provider. Mid-call, only a same-voice, same-model deployment in another region; otherwise pre-rendered hold and close clips and one unbilled callback. Carrier failover is pre-dial only, via a declared line of the same brand.
open_decisions.why: Silent fallback in tests was rejected; a same-provider alternate fails in a provider-wide outage; a mid-call voice swap breaks the experience and the run manifest.

open_decisions.question: Should the runtime split into a Python voice service and a TypeScript control plane?
open_decisions.recommendation: Yes: port the Python lab as voice-rt in Azure Central India, with the control plane in TypeScript on India-resident Postgres. Reverse if a TypeScript port matches battery latency with less operations work.
open_decisions.why: The lab's adapters, ledger, hang-up guard, Plivo line and meter are Python and measured; the product plane needs one API spec and one registry.

open_decisions.question: Do regional languages ship in v1?
open_decisions.recommendation: Five betas in v1 (Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Marathi, Bengali) on the Indic stack, each released only when its opt-out, crisis, disclosure and goodbye lexicons pass and language hold is ≥ 95%; GA in v2; dialect only by opt-in.
options: Hindi belt only in v1, said plainly
open_decisions.why: req-10. Sarvam supports 11 Indic languages; its demo held Hindi 38/40 and Tamil-English 20/20 [M CMP-08]. Safety predicates must work in each language before a single call.

open_decisions.question: Should ElevenLabs and Cartesia voices join the round-2 ear test?
open_decisions.recommendation: Yes, as benchmark rows in the whole-call blind test (small spend), so 'chosen by ear' compares against the best voices available. The default must still pass the cost, residency and speed rules.
options: Keep to Gemini, Azure and Sarvam
open_decisions.why: req-54 names Gemini and Azure first. Without the strongest voices in the test, VP cannot know how far its voice is from the best, and 'better voice' stays unknowable.

open_decisions.question: How are fixed per-workspace costs (Operator brain, tests, monitoring, support) recovered?
open_decisions.recommendation: A free trial of INR 500 lifetime per verified phone; a credited INR 1,000 first top-up; Operator fair use that scales with spend; human support priced into the tiers; no seat or platform fee.
options: Absorb everything in the per-minute margin
open_decisions.why: The earlier margins left out Operator turns, test budgets, synthetic monitoring (INR 12-36k a month), support and disputes; INR 200 a day free for 14 days was an abuse vector.

open_decisions.question: Approve the small spends needed before 2026-11-14?
open_decisions.recommendation: Approve the Plivo recharge (trial credit expires 2026-11-16), VP's own DLT principal-entity registration and trial-line A2P declaration, a VP-owned Google organisation and Vertex project, and counsel on KC8, sender status and billing.
open_decisions.why: W7 cannot run after the 2026-11-17 A2P date without VP's declared trial line; the handset battery needs a working line; production must not run on another company's account.

open_decisions.question: Who builds the v0.5 slice, and by when?
open_decisions.recommendation: Name owners for voice-rt, the control plane and design now; target 6-8 weeks to the first partner calls [I]; hold every other v1 item behind the slice's exit bars.
options: Build all nine modules in parallel
open_decisions.why: v1 as first written was the whole platform with no critical path, which the graph rejected (rejected.harvest.19).

open_decisions.question: Is assisted onboarding part of the product?
open_decisions.recommendation: Include VP Success for the first 10-20 tenants in IST hours, acting only through the same tools and ledger; track the share of tenants that reach a live campaign without it.
open_decisions.why: SquadStack's human success managers are the real 'just talk' benchmark; carrier, KYC and outcome wiring are the hardest steps for an owner on a phone.

open_decisions.question: Approve the one opening spec and how its disclosure is tested?
open_decisions.recommendation: Approve: turn 1 checks it is the right person; turn 2 in one breath gives her name, the brand, 'AI assistant' in passing and the useful fact; disclosure is repeated only if it was not heard. Test 2-3 placements on the listener panel and by hazard at the disclosure moment; wording and placement may change, presence never; no undisclosed arm.
options: Approve the spec and placement test (recommended)
AI clause in the first words of the call
open_decisions.why: req-47 (must): never deny, disclose once and lightly, never as an opener that makes people hang up. Four modules had specified four placements; disclosure only when asked would break the standing rule.
